job.style: a diary entry or letter by a student

response.passage: Dear Diary, today our science teacher, Mrs. Sharma, cleared up so many doubts about fossil fuels. I used to think coal was made from dead dinosaurs, but she explained that coal actually formed from the burial of large land plants in swampy areas millions of years ago. It was fascinating to learn that petroleum is not found in underground lakes or hollow caves, but is trapped in the tiny pores of porous rocks. We also discussed petroleum refining. Many students thought it was just filtering out dirt, but it is actually a complex process of fractional distillation to separate various useful components. I was surprised to learn that products like paraffin wax, which I thought came only from bees, are actually obtained during this refining process. Mrs. Sharma also emphasized that we must conserve these fuels because they take millions of years to form under high pressure and temperature; they cannot be recreated in a laboratory in a few days. Finally, she clarified that coal tar is not just for roads; it is a versatile material used in manufacturing synthetic dyes, drugs, perfumes, and even photographic materials. It is amazing how much science is hidden in these black, oily substances we often take for granted.
response.summary: The passage explains the true origins of coal and petroleum, correcting common myths about their formation and extraction. It also highlights the importance of refining and conservation of these non-renewable resources.
